title: GTA 6 Leaks: A Timeline Of The Events So Far
text: It's been a busy few weeks for Rockstar and Take-Two following a series of leaked GTA 6 gameplay videos and images. Beginning in mid-August 2026, an anonymous individual or group calling itself CyberLeek began publishing unreleased Grand Theft Auto 6 material. The first wave included gameplay videos and apparent images of the GTA 6 map . The situation is still unfolding, so we've got a roundup of all of the events of the most recent GTA 6 leak in chronological order, along with what the footage appears to show, and CyberLeek's communications so far. Ahead of the footage being posted more widely, several Reddit users believe that infrastructure including the main CyberLeek domain and backup spelling variants were registered as early as August 14. They also claim that a $CYBERLEEK token, liquidity pool, website, and voting program were created around August 15. August 18 Jason plays basketball The first clip was around a minute long, and showed protagonist Jason Duval outside the oceanside house that's already been seen in official Rockstar marketing material. It showed off a Focus mechanic, where making a basket increased Jason's Focus level, as shown on the HUD. It's unclear whether this Focus system is present across all of the gameplay, or only in minigames such as basketball. It was initially unclear whether the footage was genuine, but as Rockstar begin issuing DMCA takedown notices, it appeared to verify the legitimacy. CyberLeek's manifesto Accompanying the first leak were some "commandments" from CyberLeek, including: Thou Shalt Not Sell Digital Preorders Thou Shalt Not Sell Fake Single-Player DLC Thou Shalt Preserve Single-Player Content CyberLeek's clearest complaint is around digital preorders. It argues that this doesn't benefit customers since the product is a digital download that cannot sell out. GTA 6 will not be released on a physical disc , despite having physical premium editions available. Jason's road confrontation The second clip to surface on August 18, titled Random Video 1, showed Jason driving before becoming involved in an altercation with an NPC. It appeared to show that a wide variety of items can be used as weapons, including a wrench. So far, CyberLeek has only shown footage of Jason's gameplay. The map Also on August 18, CyberLeek published images purporting to show the map of GTA 6's city, Leonida. GTA mapping communities have extensively researched the images and found that numerous details line up with years of reconstructed information from Rockstar's official marketing materials. The map appears to be made up of a series of in-game screenshots stitched together to show the entire open world. August 19 Taser video A third video appeared to show Jason breaking into a facility and using a taser, which would be a new type of weapon for the series if it's in the final build. Many theorized this clip could be from 2025 at the earliest, since it featured a track by Tate McRae that was released in January 2025. It shows Jason could be capable of cloning keys or smashing windows when near vehicles. Jason also seems to collect a hat from the ground and put it on. Vehicle-health and fuel-status bars are shown, too. After a short cut away, Jason and his friend drink beers on a boat while laughing about using a VPN. Quite apt. Junkies A fourth video, titled Junkies, showed Jason kicking a police officer off a motorcycle before stabbing him and driving away on it. It showed a potential wanted level of six stars, something that didn't feature in GTA 5. He then approached a community living underneath a bridge, and as Jason's wanted level increased, a warning appeared on the UI stating that the cops are looking for him and have his description. It also showed the use of something called Zombix, which will apparently have a weaker effect on your health the more you use it. Bystanders also seem to have the ability to report your crimes. Stop Killing Games distances itself Stop Killing Games--an international consumer campaign that hopes publishers will keep purchased games in a playable state after official support ends--has distanced itself from CyberLeek and its tactics. "Using illegal means to make a point is unacceptable to us," it said. https://twitter.com/StopKilingGames/status/2089892615923622375?s=20 It also urged people to not buy the CyberLeek memecoin. "Do not send these people your money, no matter how much sympathy you may feel for their actions," it explained. The polls begin CyberLeek has a memecoin called $CYBERLEEK that appears on all of the watermarked footage. This cryptocurrency's value depends on internet speculation or attention, and CyberLeek said that its token would fund a "secret project." There's been no word so far on what that secret project might be. As an incentive for people to purchase the token, CyberLeek began running polls for users to decide on the footage they wanted to view next. Whichever poll option had the most tokens purchased against it would be the next released footage. One poll asked users to choose between a car during the day, a car at night, a motorcycle at night, or a plane during the day. The plane won, with 64.4% of the total, leading to the release of the plane video. August 20 Extended gameplay This video was the one that really got people talking, as some theorized that the leaker may have access to a playable build of the game. As Jason flew over the city in a plane, it showed the density of the environment, and added new locations. A few radio stations are scrolled through, giving a better idea of what the GTA 6 soundtrack could sound like. However, the most important moment was when the character apparently was directly controlled and used gunfire to spell "Leek" on a nearby wall. Ending threats At the same time, CyberLeek threatened to release further material, including potential story and ending spoilers, unless Rockstar and other publishers change their approach to digital games. Some of the videos feature watermarked threats such as, "No physical discs? Then more leeks!" August 21 Subpoenas Rockstar parent company Take-Two filed multiple subpoenas requesting that Microsoft and Discord assist it in discovering CyberLeek's identity by providing information on its users. One subpoena filed with the Southern District Court of New York on August 20 showed that it was issuing DMCA takedown notices in order to "obtain the identity of an alleged infringer or infringers," adding that the information would only be used to protect Take-Two's rights. Take-Two has asked Microsoft and Discord to come up with the internal records before September 4, asking for information including Discord account IDs, registration emails, IP addresses, linked connections, and more. According to Discord itself , as of the afternoon of August 24, the company has not yet been served with a subpoena. Seeking advertisers A new "Contact" tab appeared on the CyberLeek website on August 21 that stated that the individual or group responsible is looking for funds "through community support and strategic partnerships" by selling ad space on its forthcoming leaks. It stressed that this is not a "ransom," though, so that's okay. It'll set those interested back a 400 XMR (Monero) fee, which currently converts to just shy of $165,450. And that's just the fee to contact those responsible. First hypercar video The next video to surface is the first hypercar video, which shows Jason driving through the streets in the Truffade Thrax--a car that's currently in GTA Online--performing burnouts and taking part in some pretty irresponsible driving. As far as content goes, it's one of the more uneventful leaked videos, but it does give a good idea of how the city could look at sunset. August 22 Strip club teaser This video began with Jason driving the same hypercar as the previous video, with smoke coming from the tires and engine. He then pulled into a gas station, refueled the car, and ran into the shop. Jason appeared to punch the shopkeeper and steal some cash. He then robbed another gas station before crashing into a barrier and damaging the car significantly. Afterwards, Jason is seen approaching a strip club and walking in. The video's watermarked message reads, "3mil marketcap = stripclub." It was interpreted that this meant if the $CYBERLEEK coin hit a market cap of 3 million, the full strip club video would be released. The leaks just keep on coming. Strip club As teased earlier on, the next video to leak showed a strip club with Easy Rider branding, which could be the name of the establishment. It's got all of the behavior you'd expect from such a place, including large warnings to not "come on to the dancers." There are plenty of neon lights, NPCs, more leaked soundtrack titles, and Jason even uses some binoculars to get a better look at the dancers. At the end of the clip, a cutscene inside a men's bathroom is shown and Jason interacts with another NPC. August 23 Wasted Another day, another leaked video. This time, Jason drove a car to the gas station. It appears to be Jason's personal vehicle--the Vapid Ganado. An NPC is spilling fuel on the floor while talking to themselves until Jason steals his truck and drives off, running him over as he goes. As he drives off, Jason crashes into another vehicle and both of them explode. Here, we see what appears to be the GTA 6 "Wasted" screen as Jason dies. After a short cut, the video returns to yesterday's leaked footage of Jason in the urinals and a quest prompt telling him to return to Lucia. This is the first time Lucia has been mentioned in the leaked footage. Fake GTA 6 downloads There are multiple copies of an apparent 113GB GTA 6 file circulating around the internet, but it appears to be padded malware. According to Tom's Hardware , testers say the file is 99.99% empty zeroes, with the remaining space taken up by a 50KB virus. Apparently, downloading and opening that file will whitelist your entire C:\ drive in Windows Defender and kill all of your security software. Probably don't touch that, then. August 24 Yet more nudity A new clip showing leaked GTA 6 footage found its way online on August 24, showing a nudist colony in Leonida. Jason's walking around near a pool and several hot tubs while dozens of naked people dance nearby. While some of them don't seem bothered by his presence, after he looks at a woman with binoculars, she physically attacks him. The leak shows the most detailed nudity I've ever seen in a game before, which is equal parts impressive and alarming. The most notable detail though, if you can draw your eyes away from all the genitalia, is the watermark. "Do you want a Lucia-led prologue? CL has been evading spoilers," it reads. CyberLeek has put up another poll, and asked gamers to show up dressed as leeks in front of the Take-Two and Rockstar offices while holding physical game discs. As the leaks continue--with more threats being made, and Take-Two seemingly not much closer to identifying CyberLeek--if you're trying to avoid spoilers, you should consider adding filters to your social-media feeds to remove any mentions of GTA or CyberLeek. As this story continues to develop, we'll update the timeline with new events. August 25 A day at the beach After a spicy piece of GTA 6 footage showed off Vice City's citizens in their birthday suits, the new leak dialed things back a bit. Set on the beach, this clip showed off Jason cycling across the sand, weaving his way between beachgoers and seagulls. The beach itself happens to be heavily populated with NPCs, as well as a few jet skis that'll come in handy when the local fuzz requires you to make a fast getaway on water. Other environmental details include sand that leaves trails as you ride across it, seaweed from the surf strewn everywhere, and the beachfront buildings casting accurate shadows across the sand. Irony is dead Also on August 25, a clip leaked of Jason visiting a brick-and-mortar video game score , which sells physical games. The inclusion of the store is perhaps meant ironically, as GTA 6 will only be available as a digital download, with the "physical" version simply being a code in a box.

title: Latest GTA 6 Leak References Irony Of The Game Being A Digital-Exclusive
text: Yet another alleged GTA 6 leak has emerged, showing off one of the game's main characters, Jason, visiting a video game store that sells physical discs. This has prompted people to point out the irony of GTA 6 being a digital-exclusive game. In the clip, we see Jason visit a store called Game Horde where he uses binoculars to zoom in on the shelves, showing various games and consoles. "This is not about actual discs. It's about ownership. Resale rights still matter, even in a digital-only era," reads a watermark on the video. https://twitter.com/littleblass/status/2092246597329379332 GTA 6 will be sold at brick-and-mortar retailers, but the game's physical edition only includes a code in the box. The data shows that more and more people, on a percentage basis, are buying games digitally today. But a lot of people still want physical game discs, while many have also expressed concerns about game preservation concerns in a digital-only era. When the GTA 6 leaks began, the person claiming responsibility listed off various "commandments," including the following: Thou Shalt Not Sell Digital Preorders Thou Shalt Not Sell Fake Single-Player DLC Thou Shalt Preserve Single-Player Content For more, check out GameSpot's timeline of the GTA 6 leaks so far . GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The gameplay leaks have been extensive, but they don't matter and people should calm down , a former Rockstar director has said. Rockstar and Take-Two have yet to identify the person or people responsible for the leak. Whoever they may be, they appear to have access to the game. In 2022, GTA 6 suffered its first major leak of gameplay footage. The autistic 18-year-old suspect was apprehended and ordered to live in a secure hospital for life . In July this year, it was reported that the person, Arion Kurtaj, left the secure hospital and is now in a “normal prison” awaiting a new trial. While the leaks have shown a lot of new footage and revealed new insights about GTA 6, we're now just days away from Rockstar releasing official footage of the game on Netflix on August 27 .

title: The Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 Costs $1,300, And The OLED Screen Better Be Worth It
text: Almost a year after launch, the Asus Xbox ROG Ally is getting an upgrade--and a hefty price increase--in the form of the X20 model. Revealed earlier this year as part of a bundle sold with a set of XR glasses, Asus has opened preorders for the handheld gaming PC, with prices starting at an eye-watering $1,300 from the official Asus online store and Best Buy . What does an extra $300 get you? The biggest draw is the screen, as Asus has equipped this model with a 7.4‑inch 1080p OLED 120Hz HDR display. The shell is also constructed from translucent plastic so you can see the inner workings of the ROG Ally X20, and those internals include an 80Wh battery, 1TB of storage capacity, 24GB of DDR5 RAM, and Wi-Fi 6 connectivity. The X20 also features a redesigned layout meant to improve airflow and thermal efficiency, as these units can get hot while running demanding games. Asus added that it has improved the D-pad and installed TMR magnetic induction analog sticks. The unit still runs on the AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme processor, which is capable of handling modern games smoothly. If you've got $2,500 to spare, you can also grab a bundle deal that includes the ROG Ally X20, a pair of 240Hz ROG XReal X1 glasses, a Dbrand Killswitch protective case set, and a Pelican case to store everything in. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XiYNNGR4uLo That's a lot of dough for a handheld, but it's not too surprising. The global shortage of memory driven by AI has seen component prices skyrocket, and several manufacturers of handheld gaming PCs have had to adjust their prices. Earlier this year, AyaNeo suspended preorders and early-bird sales of its Next 2 handheld in response to rapidly rising costs, while console prices are also feeling the pinch . The silver lining is that the makers of retro handhelds are filling the gap for affordable gaming on the go, and these cheap units make more sense than ever in 2026. Pricing for the $1,000 Xbox ROG Ally X and its smaller-specced $600 sibling hasn't increased ( yet ), and both machines are a pretty great option for playing PC and Xbox games on the go--if you can afford them. While both devices did have some teething issues with their software, recent updates have smoothed out these problems, and the Xbox app works well as a platform for users to launch games from Microsoft's store, Steam, and more.

title: Why GTA Games Are A “Stab In The Heart,” But Also Amazing, For Ex-Dishonored Dev
text: According to industry veteran Raphaël Colantonio, who worked on the Dishonored series at Arkane before starting his own studio, GTA games are "the biggest tease" and also "the biggest disappointment" for people who love immersive sim games. "I don't mean that in an offensive way because of course who am I and who are they? They make games that sell I don't know how many thousands times more than mine and they are so incredible at doing surface simulation," he told Press Box PR . "But that’s such a stab in the heart for me when they don’t go more than surface level where there’s no long-term consequences to anything you do." GTA games, instead, offer more of a "fantastic sandbox with incredible execution, incredible cinematography, [and] great gameplay," Colantonio added. He went on to say Rockstar has a formula and that he "understands why they do it." At the same time, Colantonio said a game like Skyrim is more to his liking. He said in Skyrim, there is "just one instance of the world," so your actions have real, meaningful, and lasting consequences. "You really own your consequences as a player. Everything is playable and you have to deal with your choices for the rest of the game," he said. Colantonio was speaking about GTA games so far, and not specifically GTA 6. Rockstar has yet to share specifics on how it might have updated the formula for the new game, or if there might be further reactivity to choices players make. He theorized that Rockstar's belief with the GTA series is that offering too much in the way of choices having real, lasting consequences confuses the player too much, so the developers take a different approach. "What Rockstar basically say is, you know what? That part sucks. It’s too hard to do. It confuses players and most players won’t care at all anyway," he said. "Here’s what we will do instead. We put a guy with a question mark on their head. They have a mission for you. When you want to play the mission, we open an instance of the world in which nothing else matters than what's inside this instance. Then, because of that there is a trade off." This setup works well for GTA games, Colantonio said, because it affords Rockstar the ability to have incredible set pieces and action sequences. But, again, that's not something he's personally interested in. "People are going to be thrilled but none of it matters. That's the thing. We don't have to deal with the consequences. The players don't have to deal with the consequences. Therefore, we can push the buttons, crank things up to 11, and I totally get the draw," he said. "I totally understand why people are into it. I understand why they would be into it as developers. I understand why it sells so much but this is not my values, not that my values are not to sell a gazillion units!" He went on to say that GTA games allowing players to fail missions and try them again breaks immersion. "If you fail the mission, you find yourself back out on the street and there’s the same guy with the same question mark over his head who you click on and you’re ready to restart the mission. There’s nothing immersive to me in that," he explained. Again, Colantonio said he makes these remarks "with the greatest respect" for Rockstar and what they do. "They do things that are amazing," he said, adding that he expects to get flamed for what he's saying about Rockstar and GTA. "But no, I respect them a lot. It's just that it's not my bike," he said. Asked what he would think of Rockstar making GTA 7 an immersive sim kind of game, Colantonio joked that Rockstar should do it if they want to sell fewer copies. "It's highly respectable. It's great in so many ways. It's just not my thing, and I couldn't imagine a world where they would want me in there because I'm going to bring some bizarre stuff. They're going for more direct paraphernalia where instantly you know the gameplay. It doesn't need digestion and there isn’t anything obscure like what we do here, so yeah it's a difference like the difference between Steven Spielberg and David Lynch or whatever," he said. "One is going to sell gazillions and the other one is going to be a little more indirect and obscure and sometimes land a hit." Colantonio ended his thoughts by saying he is "really, really looking forward" to GTA 6 because he wants to see "how far they can push the instant simulation, surface simulation, because they do all that so incredibly well, and it's inspiring, and I love that." GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game has seen numerous gameplay leaks this month, and Rockstar and Take-Two are said to be hunting down the people or parties responsible . Whatever happens, Rockstar is sticking with its plans to show the game off, in an official capacity, on August 27 via an extended trailer on Netflix. As for Colantonio, he now heads up WolfEye Studios, which launched its first game, Weird West, in 2022. WolfEye is now working on a new game that hasn't been announced yet.

title: New Mario Kart World Switch 2 Bundle Coming In September, And It’s $50 More Expensive Than The Original
text: Ahead of the Switch 2's price hike in September, Nintendo has announced two new Switch 2 bundles for the US. The Switch 2 + Mario Kart World bundle ($550) launches in late September, while the Switch 2 + Nintendo Switch Sports bundle ($530) arrives alongside the game on October 22. People may recall that Nintendo offered a Switch 2 + Mario Kart World bundle when the console launched in June 2025. It was priced at $500 back then, but was subsequently discontinued. Comparisons to the new bundle are not entirely 1:1, however, as the original 2025 bundle did not include a Switch Online membership. Due to various economic pressures, Nintendo is raising the price of the Switch 2 by $50 on September 1 , bringing it up to $500. That new price is factored in to the new bundle price, which is why it's $550. The new Switch 2 + Mario Kart World bundle comes with a Switch 2, a code for the digital version of Mario Kart World, and a 3-month Nintendo Switch Online individual membership. Nintendo says the $550 price point represents a savings of $38 compared to buying each item individually, but that's not the whole story. Currently, the Switch 2 costs $450 and Mario Kart World is $80, so that works out to $530 together. You can get three months of Switch Online for $8 on Amazon , for a grand total of $538, so you can save money (about $12 before tax) by purchasing everything now as opposed to waiting for this new bundle to release. The new Switch 2 + Mario Kart World bundle. The Nintendo Switch 2 + Nintendo Switch Sports Resort bundle, meanwhile, includes a Switch 2 system, a code for a digital copy of Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, and a 3-month Nintendo Switch Online individual membership. Purchasing these items separately would cost you $28 more, Nintendo said. Say hello to the new Switch 2 bundle with Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is the newest entry in the series, featuring 12 sports at launch, including wacky new ones like thumb wrestling.
